title: Attention-based motion (Cavanagh)
summary: Cavanagh (1992): superimposed colour and luminance gratings turn in opposite directions; the luminance grating sets the global motion even when its bars are invisible, while the colour bars are seen to move only when tracked with attention. Tasks: equiluminance, motion null, thresholds, attentive tracking (Experiment 1) and speed matching (Experiment 2).
references: Cavanagh, P. (1992). Attention-based motion perception. Science, 257(5076), 1563-1565. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1523411
Cavanagh, P., Tyler, C. W., & Favreau, O. E. (1984). Perceived velocity of moving chromatic gratings. JOSA A, 1(8), 893-899.

deviations.original: a CRT whose red and green phosphors had CIE (0.608, 0.348) and (0.249, 0.602), around a yellow mean of 45 cd/m2 at (0.409, 0.488)
deviations.here: any linearised display's red and green guns, at the paper's mean (45 cd/m2) and the paper's red:green luminance split (31.7 : 68.3, derived from its chromaticities); the chromaticities, and so the cone contrasts of the '40%' colour grating, follow the display's primaries
deviations.reason: CRTs with these phosphors are not available; matching luminance is what the equiluminance and contrast definitions need

deviations.original: minimum apparent speed of the colour grating (note 10)
deviations.here: the same criterion by default (equiluminance-speed); heterochromatic flicker photometry (flicker-photometry) is offered as an alternative a session can choose with equiluminance.method
deviations.reason: flicker photometry is quicker and familiar; it is not the paper's criterion, and the paper's remains the default

deviations.here: the window's neutral grey for the inter-trial interval, then 500 ms of the bull's-eye on the yellow field before the gratings
deviations.reason: alhazen draws its own background between trials

deviations.original: observers fixated the bull's-eye; one observer's eye movements were recorded during tracking (note 5)
deviations.here: fixation is instructed; no eye tracker
deviations.reason: the paper relied on instruction for its observers; an eye-tracked check would need a rig with a tracker

deviations.here: the levels a standard 8-bit display can show (about 0.5% luminance contrast per step at this mean on the example display); the isolated-grating detection thresholds of Fig. 1C (about 0.4%) need a 10-bit or bit-stealing display
deviations.reason: common hardware; the threshold task runs but its lowest settings are quantised on an 8-bit display

tasks.title: Attentive tracking (Experiment 1)
tasks.summary: Superimposed colour and luminance gratings turn in opposite directions; a pointer marks a pair of bars for 1.0 s, the observer tracks them with attention for 1.5 s, and reports whether a 240-ms test pointer is on the tracked pair.

parameters.name: target_grating
parameters.label: Target bars
parameters.meaning: Whether the pointers mark colour bars or luminance bars; fixed for a session (half the sessions each). paper: p. 1564

parameters.name: contrast_min
parameters.label: Lowest luminance contrast
parameters.meaning: The lowest of the eight luminance contrasts. paper: p. 1563

parameters.name: contrast_max
parameters.label: Highest luminance contrast
parameters.meaning: The highest of the eight; set per observer above their tracking threshold (25 to 45% in the paper; 40% for T.W.). paper: p. 1563, note 11

parameters.name: n_contrasts
parameters.label: Number of contrasts
parameters.meaning: Contrasts uniformly spaced from the lowest to the highest. paper: p. 1563

parameters.name: color_contrast
parameters.label: Colour contrast
parameters.meaning: The colour grating's contrast, a fraction of the maximum the red and green guns allow. paper: p. 1563

parameters.name: rate_hz
parameters.label: Temporal frequency
parameters.meaning: Both gratings' rate; 2.0 Hz over 8 cycles is 0.25 rev/s. paper: p. 1564

parameters.name: bullseye_rings
parameters.label: Bull's-eye rings
parameters.meaning: Rings of the 1-deg black-and-white bull's-eye. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: pointer
parameters.label: Pointer geometry
parameters.meaning: Ends and widths (deg) of the two tapered black pointers inside the annulus. ASSUMED, not in the paper (drawn in Fig. 1A without sizes).

parameters.name: cue_duration
parameters.label: Pointer on
parameters.meaning: The pointer turns with the pair for 1.0 s. paper: p. 1564

parameters.name: track_duration
parameters.label: Tracking without the pointer
parameters.meaning: paper: p. 1564

parameters.name: test_duration
parameters.label: Test pointer
parameters.meaning: paper: p. 1564

parameters.name: pre_cue
parameters.label: Gratings before the pointer
parameters.meaning: ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: response_timeout
parameters.label: Response deadline
parameters.meaning: ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: equiluminance
parameters.label: Equiluminance
parameters.meaning: Where k (green-to-red modulation ratio) comes from: the subject's latest equiluminance-speed run by default. paper: p. 1563

outcomes.name: CORRECT
outcomes.meaning: J on the tracked pair, or F on an adjacent pair.

outcomes.name: NO_RESPONSE
outcomes.meaning: No key before the deadline; the trial is served again.

events.name: FIX_ON
events.meaning: The bull's-eye on the mean field, before the stimulus.

events.name: STIM_ON
events.meaning: The gratings appear, turning.

events.name: POINTER_ON
events.meaning: The pointer appears beside the pair to track.

events.name: POINTER_OFF
events.meaning: The pointer goes off; tracking continues.

events.name: TEST_ON
events.meaning: The test pointer appears (payload: whether it is on the tracked pair).

events.name: RESPONSE_CUE
events.meaning: The test pointer is off; keys count from this flip.

events.name: RESPONSE
events.meaning: The observer's key.

tasks.title: Equiluminance by minimum apparent speed
tasks.summary: The colour grating alone turns at 2.0 Hz; the observer sets k, the green-to-red luminance modulation ratio, where it looks slowest (the paper's criterion, note 10).

parameters.name: k_start_range
parameters.label: Starting k
parameters.meaning: Each setting starts at a random k in this range. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: k_step
parameters.label: Knob step
parameters.meaning: Factor per wheel notch or arrow press. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

outcomes.name: SET
outcomes.meaning: The observer committed a setting with SPACE.

outcomes.name: TIMEOUT
outcomes.meaning: No commit before the deadline; the setting is served again.

events.name: FIX_ON
events.meaning: The bull's-eye on the mean field, before the stimulus.

events.name: ADJUST_START
events.meaning: The stimulus appeared and the knob became live; payload: starting value and step.

events.name: RESPONSE
events.meaning: The setting was committed.
